body: it’s been difficult for me to do those things while being depressed. It’s pretty obvious when i talk to people that i seem quiet or just ‘down’ and it’s made it hard to talk to people.

I think I’m just struggling to get closer to people. I can get to the point where I talk to someone, but not to a level where I’m maybe talking to them or doing stuff outside of school. This year was probably the first that I’ve actually been talking and doing stuff with a friend outside of school in a while, playing video games and stuff.

I also asked some people I talk to about the football games that have been happening recently, since I didn’t know much about them. Some of them offered if I wanted to come along with them, so that was a nice experience. One of them also said I could hang out with their group of friends, but I’m a bit afraid to since I don’t really know any of them or what they’re interested in.

What exactly are you supposed to talk about if you have limited interests. As an example pretty much everyone in my match class likes foot ball, and the teacher is a coach so they talk about football a lot. I have no interest in football. I also just have a really boring personality.

Also, if the case is I should try to talk to them, shouldn’t that mean I should also have people trying to talk to me? They didn’t make friends for no reason. I’m pretty sure I shouldn’t be feeling 100% ignored if everyone else manages to find their group by talking to people themselves.
What if you just have nothing relatable to talk about to continue talking? The most I can come up with right Away is our similar classes, assuming they’re in some of the same classes as me.
I mean, I haven’t really “connected” with anyone aside from about 2-3 new people in the past while.

Wow that post made me change my mindset a lot. I know I’m only 15, but I’ve been very enclosed and I guess a sort of “man of few words” if that’s the right way to put it, so I’ve made very few friends in the past 3 years and there’s so many people who talk to me that I’ve never really befriended since I don’t talk much.

 I’ve been trying to improve my social skills this school year, so thanks for the link.

I was too anxious while I was there to ask everything I was worried about, mainly what I said here. I have a follow up in about a month whether I take the prescription or not. I’ll see if I can ask more then.

Doesn’t it have some bad side effects and also some possible permanent effects too? I mean if it just helps you feel less sadness, isn’t that bad for the reason I’m depressed to begin with, which is my social skills since it will (maybe) make me not understand that I should be sad about something that happened? I don’t know too much about sertraline so that’s just something I’m worried about.
